definition.title: Transit Method Lab
learning_objectives: Connect orbital alignment to whether a transit occurs, grazes the stellar limb, or misses the stellar disk.
Relate the planet-to-star radius ratio to the idealized transit depth for a uniformly bright stellar disk.
Relate period, scaled semi-major axis, inclination, and impact parameter to circular-orbit contact durations.
Read a deterministic idealized light curve while distinguishing model assumptions from real stellar photometry.

fields.name: stellar_radius_m
fields.meaning: Radius of the uniformly bright stellar disk.

fields.name: planet_radius_m
fields.meaning: Radius of the opaque planet; must remain smaller than the stellar radius.

fields.name: orbital_period_s
fields.meaning: Circular orbital period used to map phase to time.

fields.name: inclination_deg
fields.meaning: Orbital inclination where 90 degrees is edge-on.

input_schema.invalid_handling: Reject non-finite values, booleans in numeric fields, planets at least as large as the star, and orbital radii that intersect the stellar or planetary disk. No scientific input is silently clamped.

output_schema: alignment classification: full, grazing, or no_transit
first-to-fourth contact duration when a transit occurs
second-to-third contact duration only for a full transit

equations.uniform_source_flux: F(p,z) = 1 - lambda_e(p,z), using the exact uniform-source circle-overlap expression of Mandel & Agol (2002)
equations.full_duration_circular: T23 = (P/pi) * asin((Rstar/a) * sqrt((1-p)^2-b^2) / sin(i)) for non-grazing transits
equations.central_depth_approximation: delta_central = (Rp/Rstar)^2; exact maximum depth is smaller for grazing geometry

definition.sampling_policy: For a transit, sample 301 evenly spaced times from -T14 to +T14 around mid-transit so first/fourth contact occur at one quarter/three quarters of the returned window. For no transit, sample the same fixed count from -P/4 to +P/4. The browser must not resynthesize flux values.
definition.default_preset: Illustrative synthetic central transit with Rp/Rstar = 0.1 and a/Rstar = 10. It is not a real exoplanet system and carries no observational provenance claim.
assumptions: The orbit is circular and the planet moves at constant angular frequency 2*pi/P.
The stellar disk has uniform surface brightness; limb darkening is intentionally absent.
The planet is an opaque dark sphere whose projected disk is circular.
The planet radius is smaller than the stellar radius.
The input semi-major axis and period define the circular geometry/time mapping; this lab does not infer stellar or planetary mass.
The synthetic default preset is educational and is not presented as measured data for a named system.
limitations: No eccentricity, argument of periastron, precession, transit-timing variation, or additional bodies.
No limb darkening, stellar spots, granulation, flares, dilution, contamination, or instrumental systematics.
No exposure-time integration, cadence smearing, random noise, or detectability threshold in v1.
The central depth approximation (Rp/Rstar)^2 is exact for a full transit of this uniform-source model but is not a universal real-star transit-depth formula.
The light curve is a deterministic educational geometry model, not a fit to observational photometry.
A no-transit result is a valid geometric outcome, not a computation failure.

validation_fixtures.purpose: Edge-on circular geometry must produce a full transit with b approximately zero.
A geometry with 1-p <= b < 1+p must retain partial overlap but no second-to-third contact duration.
A geometry with b >= 1+p must return a flat idealized light curve and no contact durations.
A full central uniform-source transit with Rp/Rstar = 0.1 must have maximum depth 0.01.
Central T14 and T23 are checked directly against Winn circular-orbit equations 14 and 15.
Returned first/fourth contact samples have z = 1+p and zero blocked flux to numerical tolerance.
Circular zero-eccentricity geometry yields a time-symmetric projected separation and flux curve.
Non-finite, impossible-size, intersecting-orbit, period, and inclination inputs fail closed.
The strict loader rejects changed model constants or schema drift.

scientific_validation.method: Cross-check the circular impact parameter/contact-duration equations against Winn (2010), the uniform-source occultation and zero-eccentricity z(t) relation against Mandel & Agol (2002), and analytic limiting cases in focused Python tests.

tools.name: pytest
tools.role: Analytic limiting-case, geometry, symmetry, domain, and artifact-integrity regression tests.
